source.author: verg
source.text: Hic manus ob patriam pugnando volnera passi, quique sacerdotes casti, dum vita manebat, quique pii vates et Phoebo digna locuti, inventas aut qui vitam excoluere per artes, quique sui memores alios fecere merendo, omnibus his nivea cinguntur tempora vitta.
source.text_original: Hic manus ob patriam pugnando volnera passi, / quique sacerdotes casti, dum vita manebat, / quique pii vates et Phoebo digna locuti, / inventas aut qui vitam excoluere per artes, / quique sui memores alios fecere merendo, / omnibus his nivea cinguntur tempora vitta.
source.text_english: Here are those who suffered wounds fighting for their country, and those chaste priests, while life remained to them, and those pious poets who spoke words worthy of Phoebus, those who refined life by the arts they discovered, and those who made others remember them by their merit: all these have their brows bound with a snowy fillet.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: rara et sponte patet, siquando pectore ductor vulnera nota gerens, galeis praefixa rotisque cui domus aut studium mortales pellere curas, culta fides, longe metus atque ignota cupido, seu venit in vittis castaque in veste sacerdos.
reuse.text_original: rara et sponte patet, siquando pectore ductor / vulnera nota gerens, galeis praefixa rotisque / cui domus aut studium mortales pellere curas, / culta fides, longe metus atque ignota cupido, / seu venit in vittis castaque in veste sacerdos.
reuse.text_english: It is seldom open, and only of its own accord, if ever the leader, bearing in his breast the known wounds, comes forth. It is the man whose house or passion is to drive mortal cares away, whose fidelity is cultivated, and far from whom are fear and unknown desire, or the priest comes in ribbons and in chaste vesture.
